sections.heading: How to Play Shadow
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Shadow"][color=q1]Shadow Priest Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]

Shadow Priest operates on a single resource system with a single hard-hitting spender. The rotation generally adheres a basic priority and a few overarching principles with several moving parts and short cooldown abilities to keep track of. AoE is much of the same, except you deal damage to targets evenly by cleaving off a single priority target using [spell=1227280] and [spell=199484]. Shadow's rotation can be boiled down to the following. 

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
	[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=5%][icon name=Inv12_ability_priest_powerwordmadness_eye size=medium type=round color=priest inline=true][/icon][/td] 
	[td][b]Maximise Shadow Word: Madness Uptime[/b]  [resource=13] is Shadow's only resource which it uses to cast [spell=335467]. Prioritize using Shadow Word: Madness to keep your insanity from capping at 100. Keeping Shadow Word: Madness up for as long as possible will increase your damage through [spell=343690].[/td]
	[/tr]
	[/table]
[hr]
	[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=5%][icon name=spell_shadow_unholyfrenzy size=medium type=round color=priest inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b]Keep Cooldowns on Cooldown:[/b] Alongside a resource system, Shadow has a variety of short, medium, and long duration cooldowns to manage. The rule of thumb is to prioritize shorter cooldown spells over longer cooldown spells to avoid situations where you lose an overall use of an ability throughout an encounter. [/td]
	[/tr]
	[/table]
[hr]
	[table]
	[tr][td width=5%][icon name=spell_shadow_possession size=medium type=round color=priest inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b]React to Procs:[/b] Shadow has several procs like [spell=375888], and [spell=373202] which need to be reacted to and spent as and when they occur to avoid wasting potential spell casts. [/td]
	[/tr]
	[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]
[center][cta-button guide=32754 icon=spell_shadow_shadowwordpain]Shadow Priest Starter Guide[/cta-button][/center]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=q1][icon name=spell_holy_powerinfusion type=round size=medium inline=true color=q1][/icon] Shadow Priest Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]
Shadow Priest has two to three major cooldowns, depending on which Hero Talent you choose to use. 

[pad]
[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]

[tab name="Power Infusion" icon=spell_holy_powerinfusion]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=q1] Power Infusion [/color][/h3]
	Due to the talent [spell=373466], [spell=10060] can be cast on allies in order to provide them with the same buff to haste that you provide to yourself when you activate it. This means as a Shadow Priest you should be aiming to find a target for Power Infusion who is going to consistently get high value from the haste buff every 2 minutes. In some cases, you can even change your Power Infusion targets throughout the encounter or dungeon, as well as time your cooldowns around those of your allies to get the maximum benefit. However, you should always prioritize your own value and damage from Power Infusion over that of others. Make sure you are always getting the maximum number of uses possible, and timing it with your other powerful cooldowns. 
[/tab]
[tab name="Voidform" icon=Spell_priest_void-blast]

	[spell=120644] is the keystone cooldown of the [color=c4]Archon[/color] Hero Talent. This ability gains value by dealing some AoE direct damage, as well as by generating resources and procs through the [spell=453783] and [spell=454001] talents. This ability triggers over a long period of time due to [spell=453109], [spell=1272308], and [spell=449806]. This slow ramp up means you should ideally use this cooldown early on in your opener and future cooldown sequences to avoid spending time in cooldowns waiting for Halo to generate procs or deal damage.
